blocks.md:
- Bonding and non-bonding electron pairs around a central atom behave like **negatively charged clouds** that **repel each other**
- To minimise repulsion, these electron pairs arrange themselves as **far apart as possible** in three-dimensional space
- VSEPR theory follows three key rules:

  1. **All electron pairs (bonding and lone pairs) spread out as far as possible**
  2. **Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs**
  3. **Multiple bonds behave like a single bond when determining shape**
- Using the **valence shell electron pair repulsion theory (VSEPR)**, this allows us to predict:

  - The **shape of the molecule**
  - The **angles between the bonds**
- Each region of electron density around the central atom is called an **electron domain**

  - A domain may contain one, two, or three pairs of electrons

blocks.md:
**VSEPR & shapes of molecules**

Draw the shape of the following molecules and compounds:

1. Phosphorus(V) chloride
2. N(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>
3. CCl<sub>4</sub>

**Answer 1**

- Phosphorous has a +5 charge so 5 Cl<sup>–</sup> ions are needed to neutralise the charge

  - Therefore, the phosphorous(V) chloride is PCl<sub>5</sub>
- P is in Group 15 and has 5 valence / outer electrons
- Cl is in Group 7 (17) and has 7 valence / outer electrons
- All 5 outer electrons of phosphorus are used to form single covalent bonds to the 5 chlorines

  - There are no lone pairs
- So, phosphorus(V) chloride has a trigonal bipyramidal shape

![Diagram shows phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) structure; on the left, electron distribution and on the right, 3D bond angles of 90° and 120°.](assets/cf0b8f4c192a-vsepr-for-phosphorousv-chloride.png)

**Answer 2**

- Nitrogen is in Group 15 and has 5 valence / outer electrons
- The carbon in the -CH<sub>3</sub> groups is in Group 14 and has 4 valence / outer electrons

  - 3 of these electrons are already used in covalent bonds with hydrogen
- 3 of N's valence / outer electrons are involved in bonding pairs with the carbon from the -CH<sub>3</sub> groups

  - This leaves one pair of electrons as a lone pair
- So, N(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub> has a pyramidal shape

![Chemical diagram showing nitrogen bonded to three methyl groups in a trigonal pyramidal shape with a bond angle of 107 degrees.](assets/d1ecb928de14-vsepr-for-nch33.png)

**Answer 3**

- Carbon is in Group 14 and has 4 valence / outer electrons
- Cl is in Group 7 (17) and has 7 valence / outer electrons
- All 4 valence / outer electrons of carbon are used as bonding pairs with the 4 chlorines

  - There are no lone pairs
- So, the shape of CCl<sub>4</sub> is tetrahedral

![Molecule diagrams: left shows carbon bonded to four chlorine atoms with electron dots; right depicts 3D tetrahedral shape with 109.5° bond angle.](assets/57945fcb042a-vsepr-for-ccl4.png)
